title: Kisspeptin expression levels in patients with placenta previa A randomized trial

citation.title: Kisspeptin expression levels in patients with placenta previa A randomized trial

printed_heading.text: Clinical Trial/Experimental Study 1 Medicine® Kisspeptin expression levels in patients with placenta previa A randomized trial Yunus Katirci, MDa, * , Adem Kocaman, PhDb , Ayse Zehra Ozdemir, MDa

what_it_measured.text: Abstract Background: This study aimed to explore the potential influence of kisspeptin (KISS1) levels on the etiology of placenta previa
The purpose of the study was fully explained to the patients and informed written consent was obtained from the patients.

endpoint.text: Plasma KISS1 levels were determined through biochemical analysis, while genetic analysis assessed KISS1 and KISS1 receptor gene expression levels.
The concentration of KISS1 protein in the range of 62.5 to 4000 pg/mL were measured in human plasma with a sample volume of 100 µL.
This study was evaluated by the Ondokuz Mayıs University Clinical Research Ethics Committee, and approved with the number of OMÜ KAEK 2021/481 board decision dated 12 November, 2021.

reported_results.text: Furthermore, the KISS1 receptor gene expression level increased 170-fold in the placenta previa group.
KISS1 gene expression level 0.043-fold decreased in the placenta previa group (P < .001).
No statistically significant difference was detected between the subgroups in the control group (P = .795) (Fig. 1B).
The difference in the number of pregnancies between the 2 groups is statistically significant (P < .05) (Table 1). 3.2.
A significant difference was defined as P < .05 and a highly significant difference was defined as P < .01.
A statistically significant difference was observed between the control and placenta previa groups (P < .05) (Fig. 2B).
